title: Notification Settings Shortcuts
lede: People now reach notification settings from where they think of them: the inbox, the app's page in iOS Settings, and shared /settings/notifications links.

sections.heading: Side by side
sections.note: Same hosted-view test, stub inbox, forced refresh failure, xxxLarge text, iPhone 18 Pro Max. Before is clean HEAD; after adds this work only.

pairs.title: Inbox toolbar
pairs.beforeCap: Only Mark All Read. Changing what reaches you meant backing out to Profile → Settings → Notifications.
pairs.afterCap: A gear opens Profile → Notifications directly, closing the inbox on the way.

changes.was: The app's page in iOS Settings only offered system alert styles.
changes.now: It also shows 'Notification Settings', which opens our own preferences. Existing users get the link at next launch, with no new prompt.

changes.was: A /settings/notifications link fell back to the inbox.
changes.now: Universal links, wisconsin:// links, and notification hrefs all open Profile → Notifications. Other /settings pages still open nothing natively.

changes.was: Rows grouped by when they were created.
changes.now: Rows group and label by when they were sent, falling back to created, like the web inbox.

changes.h: Removed an action iOS never registered
changes.was: A GT_VIEW action identifier existed with no category using it.
changes.now: Gone; a plain tap already opens the destination.

verification: npm run ios:xcode:verify on the iPhone 18 Pro Max (isolated worktree of HEAD plus this work): drift, simulator build, full XCTest suite including new route tests, generic device build — passed
NotificationInboxTests.testInboxRecoveryCapture — passed on both before and after trees
iOS notification, deep-link, long-press, and settings source contracts — 58 passed
notes: The iOS Settings link and openSettingsFor callback can only be exercised on a device or simulator with notifications allowed; this simulator's install has not granted permission, so that path is source- and build-verified only.
Built in an isolated worktree because a concurrent Schedule refactor in the main checkout still does not compile.
'in 0s' on both sides is the stub rows being dated at render time, not a change.
